news.title: Video: Yacine Abed goal sends Algeria into the Under-17 World Cup round of 32
news.lede: Algeria's under-17 side have written a new chapter in their history after a precious and hard-fought 1-0 win over the Dominican Republic in their final group-stage match at the Under-17 World Cup. The result officially secures their place in the next round and confirms them as one of the standout emerging teams at the tournament.Friday's match was no ordinary way to close the group stage. It was an early final with no room for compromise. Both teams knew only a win would earn them a place in the next round and give their fans the joy of qualification.Algeria's players had determination written all over their faces from the opening minutes.

news.title: Sabri Lamouchi Breaks Silence on Shock Tunisia Dismissal After Just One World Cup Match
news.lede: Former Tunisia head coach Sabri Lamouchi has finally opened up about the circumstances surrounding his shocking dismissal during the World Cup, revealing that the decision to sack him had apparently been made long before he was officially informed. Lamouchi, who was dismissed after just one match in charge of the Carthage Eagles, has described the events leading to his departure, expressing surprise at how quickly the Tunisian Football Federation moved to end his tenure. Speaking about the incident, the French-Ivorian tactician revealed that he first became suspicious after waking up to several missed calls and rumours circulating about his future. “The next morning, I woke up and saw several missed calls.

news.lede: For the second year running, the Ireland U17s have reached the knockout stages of the World Cup in Doha. Ireland followed up Tuesday's 3-0 victory over Costa Rica with a commanding 3-1 win over Tanzania on Friday to book their place in the Round of 32. news.title: Stonebwoy celebrates Black Challenge’s World Cup win after GH¢100,000 backing
news.lede: Stonebwoy has celebrated the Black Challenge’s historic Amputee Football World Cup win, weeks after backing the team with GH¢100,000 ahead of the tournament. Dancehall star Stonebwoy has joined the celebrations over the Black Challenge’s historic triumph at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup, weeks after backing the team financially ahead of the tournament in Mexico. The Black Challenge beat Morocco 1-0 in the final in San Juan de los Lagos on Sunday, 22 November 2026, to give Ghana its first-ever world title in amputee football. Following the victory, the award-winning musician, born Livingstone Etse Satekla, said he was pleased that his contribution had helped inspire wider support for the team.
